artifactType: Backlog 2 Batch 027 staged manual extraction input
scope: Fixed membership S4734, S4839, S3342, S5434, S4719 only
modelNote: The skill-default GPT-5.5 runner was not selectable in this delegated workspace; the available local GPT-5 Codex model was used.

checks: All five attached live primary PDFs were downloaded once and SHA-256 matched both papers.primary_file_sha256 and paper_files.file_sha256 before inspection.

The strongest directly reported S3342 layout is All seasons / 2013/14 / 2014 / 2015/16 / 2016/17 / 2017/18 / 2018/19 / 2019/20 because the paper reports an overall 334-injury cohort plus directly printed season rows.
S4734, S5434 and S4719 self-identify as systematic reviews/meta-analyses and synthesise multiple primary studies, so no primary-cohort extraction payload is staged.
S4839 explicitly identifies itself as a four-season substudy of 14 UEFA Elite Club Injury Study teams and is classified uefa; no duplicate ECIS extraction payload is staged.

S3342 Tabs 1-4 were staged and every results table and usable figure was checked once for Tabs 5-10. Table 1 supports tissue/type counts and rates; Table 2 supports location counts and rates; Figure 1/prose supports headline severity and mechanism only where defensible.

No exposure was back-calculated from injury rates. S3342 directly reports 732 matches and rates per match/round; the rate denominator is retained as the study-specific usable denominator despite unavailable player-hours.

Pooled structured counts are transparent sums of directly printed season cells. Contact/non-contact headline counts are percentage-derived from the direct overall denominator of 334 and are explicitly documented.

studyDetails.title: Injury epidemiology in Australian women's professional football
studyDetails.journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport

participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay: elite women's professional domestic league (A-League Women)

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [physical complaint requiring medical attention and resulting in a missed A-League Women match]
definitions.incidenceDefinition: injuries per match per competition round/season
definitions.severityDefinition: mild 1 missed match; moderate 2-4 missed matches; severe >=5 missed matches

exposure.seasonLength: 12 regular-season competition rounds per team; finals excluded

caveats: The paper directly reports 732 matches and a study-specific rate per match/round, but player-hour exposure was unavailable. No exposure or count was back-calculated from rates.
All-seasons tissue and location counts are transparent sums of directly printed season cells; their season-specific modelled rates and CIs remain direct source values.
Contact/non-contact headline counts (107/227) are nearest-integer percentage-derived values using the directly reported 334-injury denominator and printed 32%/68% split.

Table 2 season cells sum to 18 head/face plus 1 neck injury, while the prose states 17 head-and-neck injuries; the directly printed table cells are retained and the inconsistency is flagged for reviewer attention.
The paper reports hip/groin and sternum/ribs/upper-back as combined source categories without a clean one-to-one schema row; those families are intentionally not forced into narrower live fields.
Illness, recurrence, days lost, and raw match/training counts are absent. Figure 1 gives trend graphics but not sufficiently precise numeric labels for defensible transfer.
